title: Thermodynamic systems and surroundings
objectives: Choose a useful system boundary; classify open, closed and ideal isolated systems; distinguish matter exchange from energy exchange.
difficulty: Beginner through application; final question is a challenge
instructions: Show reasoning and units. Use a calculator when useful. For conversions use 273.15 and 4.184 J/cal. Numeric checking alone cannot award reasoning points.

questions.prompt: Define the system and surroundings if the question asks only about the water in an open cup.
A sealed, leak-free bottle warms in sunlight. Is it open, closed or isolated? Explain.
An uncovered dish loses water by evaporation. Classify the water system and identify what crosses its boundary.
A model container exchanges neither matter nor energy. Give its system type and one reason a real container may only approximate this.
A tank initially holds 220 g of water. Add 35 g and remove 18 g. Find the final mass and classify this during the exchange.
Draw a boundary around a sealed bottle plus its contents. Mark an energy arrow entering and state whether any matter arrow is allowed under the leak-free assumption.
A closed gas cylinder has a moving piston. Can the gas exchange energy by work without exchanging matter? Explain using the boundary.
Challenge: A student calls an open, insulated cup isolated. Identify two separate checks needed before accepting that claim.
